label: Hope amid dread
summary: The world climbs back into the 'Mixed / uneasy' band at 40, pulled in two directions by the same region. The single biggest development is genuinely good: the US-led Board of Peace announced late Thursday that mediators from Egypt, Qatar, Turkey and the United States had finalised a roadmap under which Hamas will surrender its weapons in stages while Israeli forces withdraw, with a Palestinian national committee inventorying arms under an International Stabilization Force over a process that could run 200 to 300 days. Trump called it 'a monumental step toward lasting peace,' the EU's Kaja Kallas called it a 'constructive step,' and Pakistan, Germany and Belgium welcomed it — but Israel has not publicly accepted the roadmap, Islamic Jihad has reservations, Hamas says heavy-weapons disarmament depends on a Palestinian state, and at least 1,100 Palestinians have been killed since the October ceasefire began. Pointing the other way, the US-Iran war is about to escalate sharply: CBS and the Wall Street Journal report Washington and Israel are preparing one of the harshest bombing campaigns of the war, against Iranian energy infrastructure, possibly running through the weekend and timed to finish before Monday's market open. Iran's Revolutionary Guard hit two tankers transiting Hormuz under US escort and four more turned back; traffic through the strait is down from roughly 130 ships a day to a handful; a tanker was hit off Oman; and the Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia has pushed Riyadh toward a Yemen offensive and a 14-nation maritime defence alliance. Russia opened August with a mass ballistic-missile and drone barrage on Kyiv that killed at least three and wounded fifteen across five districts. Africa carries the heaviest human toll: DR Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic has reached 3,442 cases and 1,521 deaths, a 50 percent jump in a week and now the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, while 24.6 million Sudanese face acute hunger and two million face famine. Europe's fourth heatwave of the summer arrived atop more than a million acres burned — triple the average — with 300,000 displaced in France and Spain and three Greek firefighters killed. The ledger is not all grim: Wall Street closed a wild July higher on a 15 percent Amazon surge and the Dow's fourth straight winning month, ASEAN's foreign ministers demanded an immediate cessation of hostilities and the reopening of Hormuz, physicists in France and Germany built the world's first all-optical photonic time crystal, and the PRIMA retinal implant went on sale across 30 European countries after restoring reading vision to most trial patients. The headline matches the rubric formula with no adjustment.

drivers.headline: The US-led Board of Peace announces that mediators from Egypt, Qatar, Turkey and the United States have finalised a roadmap under which Hamas disarms in stages while Israel withdraws incrementally, with a Palestinian national committee inventorying and storing weapons under an International Stabilization Force and the full process running an estimated 200 to 300 days; Trump calls it 'a historic agreement,' the EU's Kaja Kallas a 'constructive step,' but Israel has not publicly confirmed acceptance, Islamic Jihad says the reports are inaccurate, and Hamas says surrendering heavy weapons is contingent on a Palestinian state

The United States and Israel are preparing one of the harshest bombing campaigns of the war so far, aimed at Iran's energy infrastructure and possibly running through the weekend, with officials discussing whether to conclude before financial markets open Monday because of the likely economic shock; Trump has not yet given the final order, and Iran has threatened to retaliate against Israeli targets and US energy infrastructure across the Middle East

Russia opens August with a mass ballistic-missile and drone barrage on Kyiv in the early hours of Saturday, killing at least three people and injuring fifteen including boys aged 13 and 17, with more than a dozen explosions heard and damage across the Shevchenkivskyi, Solomyanskyi, Darnytskyi and Holosiivskyi districts; the strike follows attacks earlier in the week that killed eight, and Zelensky is pressing Washington for a licence to manufacture Patriot interceptors, which Trump says has not been agreed

Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it struck two tankers attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz under US naval escort, with four other tankers turning back; traffic through the chokepoint has fallen from roughly 130 ships a day before the war to a handful, Tehran says it will tighten its declared closure in response to a US blockade of Iranian ports, and Brent crude — which jumped 7.9 percent to 90.74 dollars earlier in the week after Trump threatened to hit Iran hard — rose again on the news

ASEAN's foreign ministers, meeting for the 59th ministerial in Manila, issue a joint statement expressing serious concern at the renewed US-Iran hostilities and calling for 'a complete and immediate cessation,' urging all parties to exercise utmost self-restraint and demanding the restoration of safe, unimpeded and continuous transit through the Strait of Hormuz — a rare piece of collective pressure from a fuel-stressed region where China and India together take more than half the oil that normally passes through the strait

DR Congo's Bundibugyo-virus Ebola epidemic reaches 3,442 confirmed cases and 1,521 deaths, a roughly 50 percent rise in the death toll in a single week and now the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record barely two months in; nearly 90 percent of cases are in Ituri province, no proven vaccine exists for this strain, healthcare workers are striking over unpaid wages and unsafe conditions, and 63 percent of recent confirmed deaths occurred outside treatment centres — though Uganda declared itself Ebola-free on 28 July

The World Food Programme reports that 24.6 million people in Sudan now face acute hunger and two million face famine or the risk of famine, with the most extreme need concentrated in North Darfur, South Kordofan and West Kordofan and at least twenty further areas of Darfur and Kordofan at risk; fighting has severely constrained humanitarian access, both parties continue to obstruct aid and detain relief workers, and the RSF and its allies declared a parallel government based in Darfur in July

Fire weather records fall on both sides of the Atlantic as a fourth summer heatwave builds over Europe: more than a million acres have burned across the EU this year, triple the recent average, across more than 1,400 fires, with over 300,000 residents and tourists displaced in France and Spain and three firefighters killed in Greece this week; in the United States 2.6 million acres have burned, with Oregon alone at 1.78 million acres — closing on its 1.93 million acre record — and 242 million dollars spent fighting them

US stocks finish a volatile July higher, with the Nasdaq up 1 percent to 25,373.85, the S&P 500 up 0.7 percent to 7,489.72 and the Dow up 276.97 points or 0.53 percent to 52,485.03 for its fourth consecutive winning month, as Amazon surges more than 15 percent on cloud growth in its biggest single-day gain in over a decade; the rally comes despite Apple sliding about 7 percent, surging bond yields and worsening inflation worries, with the Federal Reserve holding rates at 3.50 to 3.75 percent and three officials dissenting in favour of a hike

Researchers from École Polytechnique, the Collège de France and Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf report in Nature the world's first all-optical photonic time crystal, a plasmonic metamaterial of micrometre-scale gold structures over indium antimonide that changes its optical properties trillions of times per second and cuts terahertz photon losses by more than half, opening a route to ultrafast computing, better communications and a new generation of tunable lasers

The PRIMA retinal implant — a rice-grain-sized photovoltaic chip paired with infrared glasses, and the first brain-computer interface cleared to restore form vision — goes on commercial sale across 30 European countries after receiving its CE mark, with trial patients gaining a mean 25.5 letters on the standard eye chart and 84 percent able to read letters, numbers and words again; the first commercial implants are expected in Germany shortly and a US FDA review is under way

A quieter Pacific ledger runs mostly positive: ICT ministers endorse regional artificial-intelligence principles grounded in safety and cultural values, the Solomon Islands and Hong Kong agree 30-day visa-free travel from 26 August, the Cook Islands set a general election for 12 August, six Fijian medical workers lost at sea in the Lau Group are rescued, New Zealand sends eight army instructors to train an all-female Timor-Leste platoon, and around 110 health leaders gather in Apia to push for Indigenous participation in precision medicine — against a darker note as bird flu reaches a fifth Australian state, threatening over 600 native species
